title: Étale closed/open interchange and closure-defined extension by zero
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and $X$ a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme] (locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]). Use ordinary module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] over constant ring sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] on small étale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], with inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] and open extension by zero [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]. For a cartesian square with $g:Z\hookrightarrow X$ closed [def-weil-closed-immersion], $u:W\hookrightarrow X$ open [def-weil-open-immersion], $Z_W=Z\times_XW$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and projections $v:Z_W\hookrightarrow Z$ open and $h:Z_W\hookrightarrow W$ closed, for every $A_{Z_W}$-module sheaf $L$ there is a natural isomorphism
$$u_!h_*L\xrightarrow{\sim}g_*v_!L.$$
Its specified map is the transpose under $u_!\dashv u^*$ of the inverse of $u^*g_*v_!L\cong h_*v^*v_!L\cong h_*L$.
For any locally closed immersion $a:S\hookrightarrow X$, let $C$ be its scheme-theoretic closure [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image], $j:S\hookrightarrow C$ the open immersion and $c:C\hookrightarrow X$ the closed immersion, and define $a_!=c_*j_!$. For every factorization $a=u\circ h$ with $h:S\hookrightarrow W$ closed and $u:W\hookrightarrow X$ open [def-weil-open-immersion], there is a canonical natural identification $a_!\cong u_!h_*$ restricting to the identity on $S$. If also $i:Y\hookrightarrow X$ is closed and $b:S\hookrightarrow Y$ is locally closed with $a=i\circ b$, there is a natural identification $i_*b_!\cong a_!$, where $b_!$ is likewise defined through its scheme-theoretic closure in $Y$.

source.place: Tag 0GJ1 (lemma-compatible-shriek-push-finite), closed-immersion case. Closure-factorization identification and compatibility with a further closed immersion are extracted consequences, with scheme-theoretic closure as in the parent conventions.

proof.text: Apply the finite-open comparison with $(\bar v,v,j_V,j_U)=(g,h,u,v)$. The hypothesis that $g$ is finite follows from [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite]. Thus [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-pushforward-extension-zero] gives the natural isomorphism $\beta_L:u_!h_*L\longrightarrow g_*v_!L$ on underlying abelian sheaves. Its definition [def-weil-pbc-finite-open-comparison] is the adjoint of $h_*L\xrightarrow{h_*\eta_v}h_*v^*v_!L\xrightarrow{\mathrm{Ex}^{-1}}u^*g_*v_!L$. Since the open-extension unit is invertible [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-unit-iso], this is exactly the inverse of the composite $u^*g_*v_!L\xrightarrow{\mathrm{Ex}}h_*v^*v_!L\xrightarrow{h_*\eta_v^{-1}}h_*L$, so $\beta_L$ is the transpose of its inverse under $u_!\dashv u^*$.

source.place: Tag 0GJ1, lemma-compatible-shriek-push-finite; Tag 0F70, lemma-jshriek-open; closed immersions finite: morphisms.tex, Tag 035C, lemma-closed-immersion-finite

proof.text: The preceding comparison is $A$-linear. Indeed the direct-image formula and the sheafified extension-by-zero construction [def-weil-pbc-direct-image, def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] give their usual underlying abelian sheaves. For each $a\in A$, apply naturality of $\beta$ to the abelian sheaf endomorphism $a:L\to L$: this says $\beta_L(a s)=a\beta_L(s)$. A section of the constant ring sheaf is locally represented by constants [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], so the same equality holds for every local scalar, by the sheaf axiom. This is precisely the module-morphism condition [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The inverse of a bijective $A$-linear map is $A$-linear too. The units and counits of $u_!\dashv u^*$ and $v_!\dashv v^*$ on module sheaves are given by the same presheaf formulas as on abelian sheaves [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction], and the exchange map is built from direct-image formulas, so the maps in step 1 have the same underlying abelian maps; the module inverse image uses the identified constant coefficient ring [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Hence step 1 gives the specified natural isomorphism of module sheaves, including its prescribed transpose.

source.place: Tag 0GJ1, module enhancement by naturality in scalar endomorphisms; Tag 03S3, definition-extension-zero

proof.text: Check the finiteness hypotheses for scheme-theoretic images. Write a locally closed immersion as $S\xrightarrow{h}W\xrightarrow{u}X$, closed then open, as in [def-weil-closed-immersion]. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], $W$ is Noetherian. Its closed subscheme $S$ is quasi-compact (a closed subspace of the quasi-compact space $W$), and is locally Noetherian: on affine charts its rings are quotients of Noetherian rings; ascending chains of ideals pull back to ascending chains upstairs. Every open of $S$ is therefore quasi-compact, by the same cited open-subscheme lemma. In particular $a^{-1}(V)$ is quasi-compact for every affine open $V\subset X$, so $a$ is quasi-compact. Open immersions are monomorphisms by their definition [def-weil-open-immersion], and closed immersions are monomorphisms by their local surjective ring maps. Thus $a$ is a monomorphism; its diagonal is an isomorphism, so it is quasi-separated. This argument also applies with any closed subscheme of $X$ as ambient scheme.

source.place: Tag 01R8, lemma-quasi-compact-scheme-theoretic-image, hypotheses; elementary Noetherian and immersion checks

proof.text: For $C=\operatorname{SIm}(a)$, [lemma-nagata-immersion-open-in-scheme-image] makes the factor map $j:S\to C$ open. For the chosen $W$, the base change $S\times_XW$ is canonically $S$: the inverse to its first projection sends $s$ to $(s,h(s))$. Thus the restricted morphism $a_W$ is $h$. Apply [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-restrict-open], whose quasi-compact and quasi-separated hypotheses were checked in step 3, and then [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-of-closed-immersion], to obtain $C\times_XW\cong\operatorname{SIm}(h)\cong S$ as closed subschemes of $W$. These identifications respect the factor maps: both give a map from $S$ to the same closed subscheme over $W$, and a closed immersion is a monomorphism. Consequently the square with edges $j:S\to C$, $h:S\to W$, $c:C\to X$ and $u:W\to X$ is cartesian. This proves the scheme-theoretic, rather than just set-theoretic, square needed below.

source.place: Tags 01R6/01R7/01R8, scheme-theoretic image and restriction to an open; the cited DAG immersion and closed-image consequences

proof.text: Apply steps 1 and 2 to the cartesian square in step 4 and invert its comparison. This defines, naturally in $L$, $a_!L=c_*j_!L\xrightarrow{\beta_L^{-1}}u_!h_*L$. To check its normalization, write $t_L:h_*L\xrightarrow{\sim}u^*c_*j_!L$ for the adjoint used to define $\beta_L$. The defining equation for an adjoint transpose is $u^*(\beta_L)\circ\eta_{u,h_*L}=t_L$. Under the open-unit identification $u^*u_!h_*L\cong h_*L$ [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-unit-iso] and the exchange/open-unit identification $u^*c_*j_!L\cong h_*L$ of [def-weil-pbc-finite-open-comparison], this equation says that the restriction is the identity of $h_*L$. Restrict once more along $h$; the closed-immersion left-inverse property [lem-kun-04ca] identifies $h^*h_*L$ with $L$. Its abelian statement applies to modules by the scalar argument of step 2. The resulting map is therefore the identity of $L$, as required. No unspecified isomorphism between the two extension functors has been chosen.

source.place: Tag 0GJ1, specified adjoint comparison; Tag 0F70, open units; Tag 04CA, proposition-closed-immersion-pushforward

proof.text: For the last clause put $D=\operatorname{SIm}_Y(b)$, with $d:D\hookrightarrow Y$ and $j_D:S\hookrightarrow D$. The ambient $Y$ is Noetherian by the closed-subscheme calculation in step 3, so that step and [lemma-nagata-immersion-open-in-scheme-image] give the stated open $j_D$. Since $a$ factors through the closed subscheme $Y\hookrightarrow X$, [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-universal] gives a closed map $q:C\to Y$. Its composite with $j$ is $b$, because their composites with the monomorphism $i$ agree. Applying the same universal property to $b$ factoring through $q$ gives $r:D\to C$ over $Y$. Conversely $id:D\to X$ is closed: locally it is the composite of two surjective quotient maps [def-weil-closed-immersion]. As $a=idj_D$, the universal property for $a$ gives $s:C\to D$ over $X$. Both $rs$ and $\mathrm{id}_C$ have the same composite into $X$, and both $sr$ and $\mathrm{id}_D$ have the same composite into $X$. The closed inclusions are monomorphisms, so $rs=\mathrm{id}_C$ and $sr=\mathrm{id}_D$. Hence $D\cong C$ canonically over $X$, and the open factor maps from $S$ agree under this identification.

source.place: Tag 01R6, lemma-scheme-theoretic-image, minimal closed factorization applied twice; Tag 01R8 and the cited immersion consequence

proof.text: Identify $D$ with $C$ by step 6. Direct images compose by their defining formula [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]: on an etale test object $E\to X$, both $i_*d_*F$ and $(id)_*F$ evaluate to $F((E\times_XY)\times_YD)=F(E\times_XD)$, using the canonical associativity isomorphism of fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product]. The section identifications commute with restrictions, sheaf morphisms and the constant $A$-action, and their inverses are the reverse fibre-product identifications. Thus $i_*b_!=i_*d_*j_{D!}\cong(id)_*j_{D!}\cong c_*j_!=a_!$ is the desired natural identification. The equality of the open factor maps established in step 6 identifies their extension-by-zero functors, so this comparison involves no change of the chosen coefficient category.
